conventions.convention: The lattice is Γ = Z^d with d ≥ 1. The vacuum representation permits q ≥ 1, but thermal nonnormality requires q ≥ 2.
The vacuum Hilbert space is ℓ² of configurations with finitely many nonzero labels, with reference label 0 and inner product linear in its first variable.
Normality means preservation of suprema of bounded increasing positive nets on the represented bicommutant. Extension means agreement with ω on every π(A), and normality is representation-dependent.
Countable Choice is assumed. The onsite KMS theorem explicitly carries the finite-matrix C*-identity and density/state norm interfaces as conditional premises.
Heisenberg dynamics is conjugation by e^(itH/ℏ). The bounded KMS strip has width βℏ, lower edge ω(Aα_t(B)), and upper edge ω(α_t(B)A); H has units J, β has units J⁻¹, and ℏ has units J s.

load_bearing.statement: The finite-factor local actions extend to a unital isometric *-representation π of the norm-completed quasi-local algebra on ℓ²(S_fin); normality on π(A)'' is defined by preservation of bounded increasing positive suprema.

Under Countable Choice and the exact finite-matrix interfaces [A2], for Γ = Z^d, d ≥ 1, finite q ≥ 1, h = h*, β > 0 and ℏ > 0, the consistent densities r^⊗Λ, where r = e^(−βh)/Tr(e^(−βh)), extend uniquely to a state ω_r, which is the unique β-KMS state for the onsite thermodynamic dynamics.
Assume Countable Choice, Γ = Z^d with d ≥ 1, and finite on-site dimension q ≥ 1. The finite-excitation representation π is faithful and irreducible: π(A)' = C I and π(A)'' = B(H_vac).

Assume AC_ω, Γ = Z^d with d ≥ 1, q ≥ 2, h = h*, and β > 0. The unique onsite product β-KMS state ω_r has no normal extension to π(A)'' = B(H_vac). In particular, no positive trace-class density operator represents all its quasi-local expectations in this representation.

concerns.concern: The summary says, “In a finite-dimensional onsite Gibbs model, the product state is the unique KMS state, yet it has no normal extension in this particular representation.” It omits the essential q ≥ 2 restriction. The page's definition and onsite uniqueness theorem allow q = 1; then S_fin is a singleton, H_vac = C, and the unique product state is normal. The nonnormality theorem itself correctly assumes q ≥ 2.

The Ruelle reference specifies “Chapter 2 §5, printed pp. 42–44 (commutant and irreducibility criteria)”. The linked PDF has only 36 pages; Chapter 2 §5 concerns Møller morphisms. Commutants and irreducibility are instead discussed in Chapter 1 §§4–5, printed pp. 9–10. The same erroneous locator occurs in def-qsm-vacuum-spin-representation and thm-qsm-product-thermal-state-nonnormal. Checked against [Ruelle's PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math-ph/0107009). The local mathematical arguments do not rely on this erroneous locator.

seams_checked.note: The consumer preserves the supplier's bounded physical-time strip convention and its conditional finite-matrix and completion hypotheses. The Gibbs-strip supplier is used only for local pairs, followed by an explicit norm-density extension. Onsite uniqueness is derived locally from finite-dimensional KMS uniqueness; the prerequisite page does not assert general infinite-volume uniqueness or a global density representation.
